archetypes.name: stream-placement
archetypes.rationale: The 6 new CLI mains have an asymmetric stdout/stderr contract: upsert-summary routes failure envelopes to stderr while all other verbs use stdout; read_main has a two-tier usage split (shell-level failures emit stdout envelopes, parser-level missing-option-value failures are stderr-only). Incorrect routing is invisible in happy-path tests but silently breaks any shell consumer that captures the wrong fd.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every new and modified `*_main` function in `python/tracking_issue.py` for whether failure envelopes (`FAILED=true`, `ERROR=`) and success KVs land on the correct stream as specified in the plan. Pay particular attention to (1) `upsert_summary_main` routing non-usage failures to stderr while other verbs use stdout, (2) `read_main` distinguishing shell-level from parser-level usage failures, and (3) whether `logging_util.quiet_init()` is always called before any contract output to prevent KVs from being intercepted by quiet diagnostics. Check shell consumer scripts that capture separate stdout/stderr files to confirm they expect the right stream for success fields vs failure envelopes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: consumer-cutover
archetypes.rationale: Twelve shell scripts and several SKILL.md files are being cut over from the retired shell helpers to the Python CLI. If any consumer still references a deleted helper, passes wrong flags, or misparses subtly changed KV output (e.g., RENAMED= or NEW_TITLE= field casing, error-message prefix changes), the breakage is silent and deferred to a live run.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every shell script and SKILL.md file updated in this diff correctly invokes the new `python3 .../python/cli.py tracking-issue ...` form and parses its output. Check that flag names match what `argparse` in `tracking_issue.py` actually registers (e.g., `--issue`, `--marker`, `--comment-id`). Look for any remaining references to deleted helpers (`tracking-issue-read.sh`, `tracking-issue-write.sh`, `tracking-issue-summary.sh`) in scripts, SKILL.md files, `.claude/rules/`, docs, `Makefile`, `AGENTS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `agent-lint.toml`, and `.gitleaks.toml` that were supposed to be swept. Also check whether the Makefile `.PHONY` and `test-harnesses-*` shard removals are consistent with the harnesses actually deleted (no orphaned shard entries, no missing entries). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
